title: Fppf-local algebraic-space representability with a bounded family of charts
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on the big fppf site of $T$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. Let $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering. Suppose that the sheaf $F_i=h_{T_i}\times F$ is an algebraic space over $T_i$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], for every $i$. Suppose there are representable surjective etale scheme charts $V_i\to F_i$ such that the scheme $\coprod_{i\in I}V_i$ belongs to the chosen big site; the algebraic-space coproduct under this chart condition is [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct], and scheme coproducts are [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Then $F$ is an algebraic space over $T$. In particular the size condition is satisfied when $I$ and all the charts $V_i$ are small in one Grothendieck universe and the big site contains their scheme coproduct. Here $h_Z(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_T(W,Z)$, and products of sheaves are evaluated objectwise.

source.place: Tag 04SK (lemma-locally-algebraic-space), with spaces.tex Tag 02WQ (lemma-coproduct-algebraic-spaces) for the sufficient chart-size condition.

proof.text: Put $U=\coprod_iF_i$ in fppf sheaves on $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$ and let $q:U\to F$ be induced by the second projections $F_i=h_{T_i}\times F\to F$. Each $F_i$ is given as an algebraic space over $T_i$; by part (1) of [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] for $g:T_i\to T$, the same sheaf viewed over $T$ (with $j_!$ given by the displayed coproduct formula, which recovers $h_{T_i}\times F$) is an algebraic space over $T$, and the chart $V_i$ viewed as a $T$-scheme still maps surjectively and etale to it. The supplied charts $V_i\to F_i$ and their site-valued scheme coproduct satisfy exactly [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct], so $U$ is an algebraic space over $T$. This is where the chart-size hypothesis is used.

Fix a site scheme $Z\to T$ and $a\in F(Z)$. Set $Z_i=Z\times_TT_i$ and $P_a=\coprod_i Z_i$ using [def-pc-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], in the bound of [def-weil-size-convention]. There is a natural isomorphism $h_{P_a}\simeq h_Z\times_FU$ over $h_Z$. Indeed [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition] describes a section $u\in U(W)$ by a clopen partition $W=\coprod_iW_i$ and pairs $(b_i,s_i)\in T_i(W_i)\times F(W_i)$. A section of the right hand side is $(g,u)$ with $g:W\to Z$ and $q(u)=g^*a$; this equation says exactly $s_i=(g|_{W_i})^*a$. Thus its data reduce to the partition and the maps $(g|_{W_i},b_i):W_i\to Z_i$. They glue uniquely to a map $W\to P_a$; conversely inverse images of the summands of $P_a$ recover this data. The two operations are inverse and commute with restriction, by the restriction clause of the partition lemma and uniqueness of gluing. Hence this identifies the sheaves and their projections, without using a diagonal for $F$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change], $\{Z_i\to Z\}_i$ is an fppf covering. Thus every $Z_i\to Z$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and their images cover $Z$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. The map $p_a:P_a\to Z$ restricts to these maps on its disjoint open summands. For a point of $P_a$ in $Z_i$ its source local ring and its map from the target local ring are those for $Z_i\to Z$, so it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Affine neighbourhoods witnessing finite presentation for $Z_i\to Z$ remain affine open neighbourhoods in $P_a$, so $p_a$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The union of the images gives surjectivity. This uses neither finiteness of $I$ nor quasi-compactness.

Regard the scheme $P_a$ as the algebraic space $h_{P_a}$ over $Z$ by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]; by part (1) of [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] for $Z\to T$ this is the sheaf $h_{P_a}$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$ of step 2 together with its map to $h_Z$. The scheme-comparison clause of [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] identifies the flatness and local finite presentation in step 3 with their algebraic-space meanings. Surjectivity also holds on point classes: a field-valued point of $Z$ has an underlying point in the image of some $Z_i$; a common residue-field extension of this field and that of a point above it gives a lift representing the same point class. Steps 1--3 therefore verify every scheme-test hypothesis of [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap] for $q:U\to F$. Apply that theorem to obtain that $F$ is an algebraic space. The final sufficient size condition of the item is precisely its assumed site membership of the chart coproduct: a small family of small schemes has a small disjoint union, and the stated big-site containment supplies the remaining condition.
